content.text: {"headline":"Recommend no action (P0): service level is predicted at 94.6% for 16:45-18:45, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The payments spike is tied to P1 incident INC-20261001-6607 (card authorisation gateway, debit cards declining). From 13:30 to 14:15, card_declined calls ran 7.35x normal and made up about 300 of the roughly 400 extra calls. Even so, with current staffing the disruption window is forecast at 94.6% overall. That is 93.5% on payments and 96.1% on general, with a 1.4% abandon rate and 88.1% for the rest of the day. General's recent dip (35-65%) looks like small-queue noise or overflow from payments, not a separate problem: volume is only 1.5% over forecast, handle time is under forecast and staffing is on plan. No escalation is flagged.","trade_offs":["P1 (agent moves plus callback, no cost) predicts a slightly lower 93.9% and pulls general down from 96.1% to 94.7%, so it adds risk to general for no gain.","P2 and P3 predict higher service levels (97.7% and 97.9%, abandon rate 0.7% and 0.6%) for INR 204. Both break policy CX-01, because the outage message must target only rising reasons on payments and the forecast shows none rising in this window.","P0 accepts a slightly higher abandon rate (1.4%) and slightly lower payments service level (93.5%) than the outage-message plans, but stays within policy and costs nothing."],"watch":"Watch payments arrivals and card_declined volume while INC-20261001-6607 stays open. If calls start rising again, or payments service level heads towards 80%, revisit the options. P1 is the no-cost fallback, and the outage message would comply with CX-01 once card_declined is actually rising. Also check that general recovers rather than continuing to dip."}
